title: Resilience beyond diagnosis: prospective neural correlates of better-than-expected outcomes in depression
title_zh: 超越诊断的韧性：抑郁症中更佳预期结果的前瞻性神经相关性
abstract: Abstract Resilience, the ability to adapt positively in the face of adversity, is shaped by combined influences of risk and protective factors. Previous neuroimaging studies on resilience have predominantly focused on single factors, often operationalizing resilience dichotomously as the absence of psychiatric disorders despite adversity. In this prospective magnetic resonance imaging study, we defined resilience as “better-than-expected” depressive symptom severity (Hamilton Depression Rating Scale) relative to cumulative risk across 22 risk and protective variables. Using ridge-regularized regression in N = 1804 participants (955 healthy, 849 depressed) from the Marburg-Münster Affective Disorders Cohort Study, we predicted symptom severity and derived residuals as measures of resilience. Residuals were then used to predict gray matter volume (GMV) and cortical thickness at baseline (T1) and two-year follow-up (T2; N = 808). This approach was complemented by extreme-group comparisons of resilient (better-than-expected outcome) and vulnerable (worse-than-expected outcome) individuals. Cumulative risk explained 49.6% of variance in depressive symptoms at T1 and 40.1% at T2. Residual scores showed moderate temporal stability ( r = 0.32, p < 0.001). Region-of-interest and whole-brain analyses revealed no morphometric associations with resilience at T1. In contrast, higher resilience at T1 predicted lower GMV in the left inferior orbitofrontal gyrus (IOFG) and temporal pole at T2 (ROI, p FWE(peak) <0.001, r partial = 0.18), with no changes in cortical thickness. Taken together, resilience to cumulative risk, defined as better-than-expected depressive symptom severity, was not associated with immediate brain structural differences. However, prospective analyses revealed smaller GMV in the IOFG and temporal pole over time, potentially reflecting greater neural efficiency or delayed biological costs.
abstract_zh: 摘要：韧性，即在逆境中积极适应的能力，受到风险与保护因素共同影响。以往关于韧性的神经影像研究主要聚焦单一因素，常将韧性二元化为在逆境中仍无精神疾病的状态。本前瞻性磁共振成像研究将韧性定义为相对于22项风险与保护变量累积风险而言，抑郁症状严重程度（汉密尔顿抑郁量表）“优于预期”。在马尔堡-明斯特情感障碍队列研究中，使用岭回归对N=1804名受试者（955名健康，849名抑郁）进行预测，得到症状严重程度的残差作为韧性指标。随后将残差用于预测基线（T1）和两年随访（T2，N=808）时的灰质体积（GMV）和皮层厚度。该方法还辅以韧性（优于预期结果）与易感（劣于预期结果）个体的极端组比较。累积风险解释了T1时抑郁症状方差的49.6%和T2时的40.1%。残差得分显示中等的时间稳定性（r=0.32，p<0.001）。ROI和全脑分析未发现T1时韧性与形态学的关联。相反，T1时更高的韧性预测T2时左侧下丘脑前额叶回（IOFG）和颞极的GMV降低（ROI，p FWE(peak)<0.001，partial r=0.18），但未见皮层厚度变化。综上所述，定义为“优于预期”抑郁症状严重程度的韧性与即时脑结构差异无关。然而，前瞻性分析显示，随着时间推移，IOFG和颞极的GMV减小，可能反映更高的神经效率或延迟的生物学成本。
